summary: Detected 3 high-confidence algorithmic blind spots across 37 analyzed submissions. Primary failure mode is off-by-one boundary handling in Binary Search, followed by improper DP state definition and BFS queue inflation.

weak_topics.description: Consistently terminating with left < right instead of left <= right, or improper mid-pointer updates that skip valid boundaries.
Assuming greedy prefix transitions, omitting exponential recursion memoization, and off-by-one 0-index base cases.

weak_topics.failure_mode: Visited State Tracking & Disconnected Component Omissions
weak_topics.description: Marking visited states post-pop rather than on push in BFS (causing memory explosion), and failing to iterate disconnected components.
Left pointer regressing on stale hash entries and using 'if' instead of 'while' when shrinking window boundaries.

recommended_problems.title: Binary Search
recommended_problems.reason: Reinforce strict left <= right loop invariants and exact target matching on single-element boundaries.

recommended_problems.title: Search Insert Position
recommended_problems.reason: Practice lower_bound invariant preservation when target is not present in array.

recommended_problems.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
recommended_problems.reason: Build intuition for precise 1D DP state formulation dp[i] = length of LIS ending strictly at index i.

recommended_problems.title: Number of Islands
recommended_problems.reason: Master immediate queue-enqueue visited marking in 2D grid BFS to prevent redundant node expansions.

recommended_problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
recommended_problems.reason: Fix window shrink logic using left = max(left, seen[char] + 1) to prevent left pointer backwards traversal.
